title: Sharp Limits for Testing Adiabatic Elimination in Raman Pulses
content: A Raman pulse can transfer the entire population while a symmetric timing probe reveals nothing of the eliminated dynamics. Reliable validation therefore requires probes chosen to expose model error. We derive the globally optimal symmetric timing contrast and an endpoint preparation theorem for matched couplings, with an exhaustive certificate for the exact optimum of a worked family. For independently calibrated two-level responses, we determine sharp joint limits on recording error and advance information about the setting. Under explicit conditions, a weighted binary score reaches the bounded-error boundary, where the two model classes can generate the same complete recorded law. These limits identify which errors can be overcome by more data and which make the descriptions indistinguishable. For a certified Raman design with 90% detection efficiency and differential recording errors of radius 0.1%, we also determine the exact minimum fixed number of attempts for 1% false rejection and 90% power under the specified fair-setting protocol. With individually bounded errors and imperfect setting randomness, the weighted score reduces a worked count by 32.2%. The results connect pulse design, calibration and finite-data inference through analytic proofs and independently verifiable certificates.
